newsitem.title: UK: World coffee use could fall as price rises - analyst.
newsitem.headline: World coffee use could fall as price rises - analyst.

text.p: World coffee use could fall by 1.7 percent in 1997 from 1996's 75.5 million 60-kg bags as current high bean prices suggest real retail prices this year should be 10 percent higher than in 1996, a veteran UK coffee analyst said.
Kerry Muir, writing in the April 25 issue of F.O. Licht International Coffee Report, said a 20-percent rise in prices on the supermarket shelves would cut consumption by five percent.
A 1.7 percent drop in consumption was seen as fairly modest in volume terms, though competition was likely to intensify among roasters, particularly in western Europe, Muir said.
"Roasters and packers of supermarket own-label may gain..." he added.
World green coffee prices had started to climb again after falling in mid-March following the blistering rally seen since early January.
Prices of New York's arabica coffee futures rose by more 50 percent between January and March on supply disruptions from Colombia and expectations of lower Brazilian crop.
The rally led to announcements of retail price increases by some major western roasters.
Muir said European consumption could fall to 41.6 million bags from 42.2 million based on a 10 percent increase in consumer prices.
He said the coffee consumption trend also hinged on other key factors besides the retail prices.
These factors included the price of close competitors to coffee such as tea, milk, fruit juices and carbonated drinks.
Other considerations included the level of disposable income.
